- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then drop sharply, suggesting overshoot after initial spikes.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias — forecasts often revert to historical mean too quickly, missing sustained trends.
- Late-period forecasts (last 5–10 days) are often too low, indicating underestimation of downward momentum or delayed correction.
- Model fails to capture sharp downward corrections after spikes — tends to underestimate price drops following high peaks.
- Forecasts show lag in responding to recent price declines — often takes 2–3 days for model to adjust downward.
- Overconfidence in short-term momentum — forecasts overreact to recent volatility without sufficient smoothing.
- Model underestimates the impact of policy or market shocks — fails to adjust forecasts downward when external factors (e.g., emission caps, regulatory changes) are present.
